solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: European resort, sewer coming up beneath it

indicators.note: in a down entry, the second piece sits beneath the resort piece just named

parts.note: a spa is a health resort

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a drain carries sewage away, so it is a sewer

explanation.surface: A grim holiday town where a sewer bubbles up right underneath it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European' is a noun here, a person from a European country; 'coming up' only works because the entry runs down the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spaniard is a native of Spain, a European country, so the noun European covers him.

clue.text: Dread the ultimate in government failure

indicators.note: the ultimate letter in a word is its final one, so take the end of government

parts.note: an error is a mistake or failure

explanation.surface: A citizen fears that the worst outcome is the government collapsing.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name intense fear, so dread and this noun are synonyms.

clue.text: Desire is coming between extremes of wrath

indicators.note: is is placed between the two outer letters, cutting them apart
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters, here W and H

explanation.surface: Longing that sits halfway between two bouts of fury.
explanation.definitionFit: To want something is to have a longing for it; desire and this noun are synonyms.

clue.text: Try to keep story up — it's ice-cream!

indicators.note: the try word holds the reversed story inside it

parts.note: to have a go is to try

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: An exclamation from someone straining to keep a tale going, then spotting dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try' is a noun here, a go, not a verb; 'up' reverses the story only because the entry runs down.
explanation.definitionFit: Gelato is Italian-style ice cream, so it is a type of the dessert named.

clue.text: Fresh, in water off the Isle of Wight

parts.words: water off the Isle of Wight
parts.note: the Solent is the strait between the Isle of Wight and mainland southern England

explanation.surface: Swimming in cold sea off an English holiday island is bracing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresh' reads as a description of the sea, but in its sense of cheeky it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Fresh can mean cheeky or impertinent, so a rude, disrespectful manner fits it.

clue.text: Footballer seeking victory over Germany, but losing many!

indicators.note: in a down entry the victory piece sits over the rest

parts.note: a win is a victory

indicators.note: Germany loses the letters of the word many, leaving its first three

parts.note: the full country name, from which a word is then removed
taken as written, the word removed

explanation.surface: A footballer chasing a win against Germany, though his side concede a lot of goals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing many' strips MANY from GERMANY, leaving GER.
explanation.definitionFit: A winger is a footballer who plays on the wing, an attacking position on the flank.

clue.text: Opening found in Coventry

indicators.note: says the answer is a run of letters sitting inside the city name

explanation.surface: A gap or vacancy turning up in an English city.
explanation.definitionFit: A vent is an opening for air or gas to escape through, such as a flue.

clue.text: Are settled on power, to be in authority

indicators.note: in an across clue, the second piece follows on after power

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for power in physics
to reside is to live in a place, so are settled = reside

explanation.surface: People who have made their home where power lies, to govern from there.
explanation.definitionFit: To preside is to chair or hold control over a meeting or body.

clue.text: Buzz, as first of insects enters hooter

indicators.note: the single letter goes into the nose word

parts.note: hooter is British slang for a nose

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of the word insects

explanation.surface: A buzzing sound as an insect flies up someone's nose.
explanation.definitionFit: A buzz is a kind of sound, so it fits the general word for sound or din.

clue.text: Thorn, nasty point!

indicators.note: something nasty is in a bad state, so the word thorn is mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone pricked by a thorn complains about its sharp tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point' reads as a thorn's tip but means a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the four cardinal compass points, so point is a broader term for it.

clue.text: Within a day, ghost leaving house

parts.note: Mon is the short form of Monday, a day

indicators.note: the house letters leave the word ghost, leaving three

parts.note: taken as written, before letters are removed

explanation.surface: Within twenty-four hours, the spectre has departed the haunted house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes HO out of GHOST, giving GST.
explanation.definitionFit: Within a group and among it are near-synonymous prepositions meaning in the midst of.

clue.text: Refurbish a red room close to staircase, landing here?

indicators.note: refurbishing remakes a thing, so these letters are rebuilt in a fresh order
the close of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Decorating advice: redo the red room next to the stairs, and the landing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'landing' looks like the top of the stairs, but here it is aircraft touching down. 'Refurbish' rearranges A RED ROOM into AERODROM.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerodrome is an airfield, the place where aircraft land, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Funny comedian, seemingly possessed

indicators.note: something funny is odd or peculiar, so the letters of comedian are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wild-eyed stand-up comic appears to be under a spell.
explanation.definitionFit: Demoniac describes someone frenzied as if inhabited by a demon, so seemingly possessed fits.

clue.text: Really and truly, all leaders vermin!

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their first letters, taken from each of the three words

explanation.surface: A cynic sneers that every one of our political leaders is a pest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' looks political, but means initial letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Rodents of this kind are a classic example of vermin, though vermin is plural in sense.

clue.text: The turn inspiring a performer on stage

indicators.note: read as in-spiring, breathing in: the turn word takes the letter a inside it

parts.note: a spin is a turn or rotation

explanation.surface: A dancer's pirouette inspires an actor in the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A thespian is an actor, after Thespis, the legendary first actor of ancient Greece.

clue.text: A failure going back and forth

definitions.note: a thing that fails to work, and this word also reads the same in both directions

indicators.note: the word reads identically in both directions, a palindrome

parts.note: a thing that fails to work, and this word also reads the same in both directions

explanation.surface: A wasted effort that just went round in circles.
explanation.definitionFit: A dud is something that fails to work, like a shell that does not explode.

clue.text: Energetic type getting Monday off

indicators.note: off means wrong or out of order, so the letters of Monday are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bustling worker who gets the start of the week off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting Monday off' reads as a day's holiday, but 'off' signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynamo is a generator, and figuratively a tirelessly energetic, forceful person.

clue.text: Came south after breaking handlebar?

indicators.note: breaking smashes the words apart so their letters can be reassembled

explanation.surface: A cyclist headed downhill after the handlebar snapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'handlebar' looks like part of a bicycle, but it names a style of facial hair, so it is an example, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A handlebar is a style of moustache with long, upturned ends, an example of the type.

clue.text: Irish region taking part of Istanbul's territory

indicators.note: taking part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An Irish area seizing a piece of a Turkish city's land.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulster is one of the four historic provinces of Ireland, largely now Northern Ireland.

clue.text: Tooth circular initially, then a square

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of the word circular

parts.note: nine is a square number, three times three

explanation.surface: A dentist describes a tooth as first round, then box-shaped.
explanation.definitionFit: A canine is one of the pointed teeth between the incisors and the premolars.

clue.text: Crazy bunch?

definitions.meaning: going ... is slang for going mad, so crazy
fruit of this kind grows and is sold in bunches, so a bunch is a group of them

explanation.surface: A wild gang of people.
explanation.definitionFit: The fruit grow in bunches, and slang uses the same word to mean mad.

clue.text: A lot of money for a weapon

definitions.meaning: costing a ... is British slang for very expensive
an explosive device dropped or planted

explanation.surface: Paying a fortune to buy arms.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang calls a large sum a bomb, and the word also names an explosive weapon.

clue.text: Model, leg in traction?

parts.note: pins is slang for legs, so a leg is a pin
a broken leg in traction is hoisted up

explanation.surface: A fashion model in hospital with a broken leg strung up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pins' is informal British slang for legs.
explanation.definitionFit: A pin-up is a glamour model whose photo is pinned up on a wall.

clue.text: Light touch over hard course

indicators.note: in a down entry the pat piece sits over the hard letter

parts.note: a pat is a light touch with the hand
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A golfer's gentle putt over a firm course.
explanation.definitionFit: A path is a route or way taken, so it is a course in the sense of direction.

clue.text: Mother trapping black snake

indicators.note: the mother word holds the letter inside it

parts.note: mama is a childish word for mother
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A mother catches a dark serpent.
explanation.definitionFit: The mamba is a fast, highly venomous African snake, black or green.

clue.text: Land turning into sea

indicators.note: turning changes the order of the letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Coastline being reclaimed by the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning into sea' reads as a flood; 'turning' signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Estonia is a Baltic country, and land is a general word for a nation.
